conviction_note: No pre-release, no profit warning and a guide that both the company (July) and Inderes say will be reiterated, so the move is mostly the quarter itself: my own seasonal arithmetic on the Q2 actuals puts adjusted EBITDA near Inderes' 15.3 MEUR rather than the 14.7 MEUR consensus column, Finnish bank-barometer credit demand rose in Q3, and the last four prints all rose 2.2-5.9%. Against that, the Swedish licensing cliff of 1 August and an exiting former 5% holder. The bar is disputed (Inderes 12.8 vs consensus 11.5 MEUR adj. EBIT), so the findings are capped small and p_up sits at 58; abs_move 4.0 x (2*0.58-1) = +0.64, close to the findings' sum of +0.6.

already_public.what: FY2026 guidance, specified 17 July: net sales +0-5% at comparable FX, adjusted EBITDA up y/y with adj. EBITDA growth exceeding net sales growth. H1 adj. EBITDA 28.1 MEUR (+8.9% comparable), Q2 adj. EBITDA 14.6 MEUR (36.5% margin), adj. EBIT 11.6 MEUR
Report date and time: 29 Oct 2026 at about 11:00 EET (in session), webcast 13:00 EET
Pre-silent-period analyst call held 23 Sep 2026; recording public on the company site; a forum reader characterised it as 'cautiously positive'
EUR 180m syndicated refinancing (150m term loan + 30m RCF, 3+1+1 years) replacing the 2022 facility of the same size; RCF unutilised
Inderes Q3'26 preview: revenue 38.6 MEUR, adj. EBITDA 15.3, adj. EBIT 12.8 (33.1%), reported EPS 0.30; consensus column 38.5 / 14.7 / 11.5 / EPS 0.27; guidance expected reiterated

new_in_release.expect: Q3 adj. EBITDA about 15.0-15.3 MEUR on Q2 actuals plus the usual Q3 margin step-up (+2.5pp in 2025) and a full quarter of the May headcount savings: above the 14.7 consensus column, in line with Inderes. Slightly up.
Reiteration most likely (company 'specified' it in July; Inderes sees no risk). A narrowing toward the upper half of the 0-5% sales range is possible but unsourced. Flat to slightly up.

Board decision on the AGM-authorised additional dividend of up to EUR 0.50; last year the equivalent second-instalment decision was released at 08:15 CET on the Q3 day. Full payment is the expectation (Inderes DPS 1.00), so only a cut would move the stock.
Commentary on Swedish consumer volumes after the 1 August licensing cliff, and on Finnish demand. Unknown sign; the July report called the Swedish effect 'modest'.
Unknown; H1 FCF 19.8 MEUR (13.6), leverage 2.5x. No sign of a working-capital issue.

bar: Disputed. Consensus column on the Inderes preview page: revenue 38.5, adj. EBITDA 14.7, adj. EBIT 11.5 MEUR, EPS 0.27; Inderes' own estimate 38.6 / 15.3 / 12.8 / 0.30 (https://www.inderes.fi/en/analyst-comments/enento-group-q326-preview-earnings-improvement-continues, 2026-10-20). Two sources that disagree by about 11% on adj. EBIT, so every finding that depends on the bar is capped small. print_vs_bar_pct is measured against the consensus column.
session_check: bmo (for the window) - the issuer's own notice says the interim report comes out on 29 October 2026 'approximately at 11:00 AM EET', which is an hour into the Helsinki session (opens 10:00 EET), with the webcast at 13:00 EET. Release and reaction both fall inside close(2026-10-28) -> close(2026-10-29), so the bmo close-to-close window is correct; it is NOT amc. https://view.news.eu.nasdaq.com/view?id=b944ee5b002eddb78d2fb081d6cee63a0&lang=en&src=listed
positioning_check: Finanssivalvonta register read 2026-10-26 (https://www.finanssivalvonta.fi/api/shortselling/datatable/current) does not name Enento: short_ratio 0.0 is the 0.5% truncation floor, not a measurement, and anchor_covered is false, so there is no positioning anchor and priced_lean_pct (-0.02) is effectively the flat run-up (20d +0.4%, 5d -0.26%). Building/covering is unknown. The one visible flow: Long Path Partners went below 5% on 7 Oct (4.88%), an exiting holder.

findings.finding: Enento's own Q2 actuals and Q3 seasonality point to Q3 adj. EBITDA of about 15.0-15.3 MEUR (Q2 14.6 at 36.5% margin; Q3'25 margin was 2.5pp above Q2'25; the 36 headcount reductions completed in May give a full quarter of savings in Q3), above the 14.7 / 11.5 MEUR adj. EBITDA / EBIT consensus column and in line with Inderes' 15.3 / 12.8.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Profitability beats were bought on all four of the last prints: Q3'25 +2.86% (2025-10-29), FY25 +2.81% (2026-02-13), Q1'26 +5.87% (2026-04-28), Q2'26 +2.21% (2026-07-17, where Inderes said operating profitability beat its forecast). Earlier misses: 2025-07-15 -2.48%. Yahoo daily closes.
findings.why_not_priced: The stock sits at 15.12 EUR, flat over 20 and 60 days (+0.4%, -0.8%), on about $258k a day with three or four covering brokers; if the market held Inderes' number rather than the 11.5 consensus column the dispersion would not exist. But Inderes is the most-read source on this name and published the higher number on 20 Oct, so part of it is in the price. That is why the finding is capped small.
findings.independence: Inderes' own preview reaches the same level from its segment model (https://www.inderes.fi/en/analyst-comments/enento-group-q326-preview-earnings-improvement-continues); Nordea raised its target to 21.00 from 20.00 with Buy on 7 Oct per Kauppalehti, relayed on the Inderes forum (https://forum.inderes.com/t/31229/last.json).

findings.finding: Finance Finland's bank barometer (published 11 Sep, August survey) says household and corporate credit demand rose clearly in Q3 2026 against last year and beat bank managers' expectations, which supports Finnish consumer and business credit-information volumes, Enento's largest country (Inderes models Finland at only +2%).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2'26 Finnish growth of 1.7% with flat consumer volumes came in a +2.21% day. No clean history of a Finnish volume surprise on its own.
findings.original_quote: Sekä kotitalouksien että yritysten luotonkysyntä on piristynyt selvästi vuoden kolmannella neljänneksellä viime vuodesta ja jopa ylittänyt pankinjohtajien odotukset (Both household and corporate credit demand picked up clearly in Q3 against last year and even exceeded bank managers' expectations).
findings.why_not_priced: It is a macro-to-company proxy: the company has not said its Finnish consumer volumes turned, and in July it said improved confidence 'is not yet visible in our consumer credit information volumes'. Inderes still models only 'a slight pick-up'. If it were priced, Finland estimates would sit above +2%. Note that FA's chief economist quoted in the release, Veli-Matti Mattila, also chairs Enento's board; that does not change what the banks reported.
findings.independence: An Inderes forum post of 2026-09-11 picked up the same barometer (https://forum.inderes.com/t/31229/last.json); no company or counterparty confirmation.

findings.finding: Sweden's consumer-credit licensing cliff hit on 1 August 2026: of about 50 consumer credit institutions only 17 applied for a new licence and 'a clear majority' leave the regulated market. All the large loan brokers (Sambla licensed; Lendo, Zmarta and others pending) may keep operating while FI reviews them. That is a mild drag on UC's Swedish consumer credit-check volumes in Aug-Sep, the first quarter under the regime.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Swedish regulatory risk was the theme of the weak 2025 prints (2025-07-15 -2.48%); since the July 2026 statement that the effect is 'modest' the stock has not reacted to it.
findings.original_quote: Av det femtiotal konsumentkreditinstitut som berördes av kravet har 17 ansökt om nytt tillstånd sedan december 2025 ... En klar majoritet av konsumentkreditinstituten har inte sökt nytt tillstånd och lämnar därmed den reglerade marknaden. (Of the roughly fifty consumer credit institutions affected, 17 have applied for a new licence ... a clear majority have not applied and so leave the regulated market.)
findings.why_not_priced: The company told the market in July the effect would be modest because the largest brokers applied, and Inderes expects Swedish consumer information to keep recovering (+4%). So the drag sits inside what was guided and is sized near zero; it is filed because Q3 is the first quarter that shows it and the exit count is larger than was known in July.
findings.independence: Enento's own H1 report: 'we are seeing largest loan brokers as well as some smaller ones applying for licenses and therefore we expect the effects on Enento's business to be moderate' (https://view.news.eu.nasdaq.com/view?id=b4585daed600725d7088d89e098efbb80&lang=en&src=listed).

findings.finding: Long Path Partners (previous notification 5.02%) dropped below 5% (4.88%, 1,156,558 shares) on 7 Oct 2026 without any visible block trade, and was not among the three largest holders at 30 Sep. An exiting seller with about 1.16m shares left is supply overhanging a $258k-a-day name.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock rose 0.67% and 0.80% on 8-9 Oct after the flagging and has held 15.0-15.5 since.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: public since 8 Oct and the price absorbed it. What is not visible is whether the remaining 4.88% is being sold into any post-print strength, which would cap an upside reaction on a thin book.
findings.independence: Nomination Board release of 26 Oct lists Otava, SEB AB and Nordea as the top three at 30 Sep (https://view.news.eu.nasdaq.com/view?id=bdc5f7a70333c7fa8c944f09226550529&lang=en&src=listed); Inderes forum readers found no block trade (https://forum.inderes.com/t/31229/last.json).

findings.finding: The AGM authorised the board to pay an additional dividend of up to EUR 0.50 per share, and last year the equivalent decision was released on the Q3 morning (2025-10-29 08:15 CET). With H1 FCF of 19.8 MEUR, leverage of 2.5x and the debt refinanced on 31 Aug, full payment (about 11.8 MEUR) looks funded and is what Inderes models (DPS 1.00).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2025-10-29: the second-instalment decision went out with the Q3 report and the stock rose +2.86% on the day, so the decision cannot be separated from the print.
findings.why_not_priced: Full payment is the expectation and in the price (6.6% yield). The asymmetry is downside only if the board pays less than 0.50, and refinanced debt plus strong FCF make that unlikely, hence the near-zero size.

outside_window.finding: Swedish credit-intermediary register law amendments and a new licensing requirement for subsidiary credit intermediaries take effect 20 November 2026; FI decisions on the pending Lendo/Zmarta applications are undated.
CIO Annika Rådeström leaves 31 Dec 2026 and a new CTO role is being recruited for AI investment. Operating cost implications land in 2027.

baseline_tension: The lean is flat (-0.02, a run-up of +0.4% and a truncated-zero short register), so the mild positive I found neither agrees with nor fights a priced view; the only cross-current is Long Path's exit, which argues for a capped upside.
language_note: Finnish: the Finance Finland bank barometer (STT Info, 11 Sep) showing household and corporate credit demand clearly up in Q3 and above expectations. It appears in no English Enento coverage.

Finnish: the Inderes forum carried the 23 Sep pre-silent analyst call recording link, the Nordea target raise (via Kauppalehti) and the shareholder debate over Long Path's exit. None of it is in the English wire.

Swedish: Realtid's 6 Aug count of the 1 August licensing cliff (17 of about 50 consumer credit institutions applied; the major brokers operate pending review) is the only quantified read on UC's Swedish counterparties since the company's July statement.

lessons_applied: abs_move_pct raised from 3.5 to 4.0: the period is not pre-released ('you were right about the number and too small about the move'; the European median is 7.4% when numbers are new and 2.3% when the guide is reiterated, so 4.0 sits between them and above the name's ~2.8% report-day median). This moved expected_move_pct from 0.56 to 0.64.
session_check rewritten to open with the verdict and the issuer's timestamp (11:00 EET, in session, so the close-to-close window is right).
